Signature Architectural Decisions & Engineering Rigor

Why every repository prioritizes deterministic invariants, threat modeling, and reproducible benchmarks over fragile black-box wrappers.

Why Cyber Dragon Refuses to Fetch URLs

URL scanners that perform outbound HTTP fetches become SSRF proxies and trigger attacker tracking beacons. Cyber Dragon scores phishing domains, IDN homographs, and predatory USSD strings (*165#, *185#, *334#) 100% lexically in 0.28 ms with zero network egress.

Why FlowLedger Bans IEEE-754 Floats

Floating-point arithmetic silently drops cents and shillings during fee splits. FlowLedger enforces bigint minor-unit double-entry postings across UGX, KES, and USD with SHA-256 hash-chained journal entries (97 entries verified with 0 imbalance).

Why Auralis Binds Only to 127.0.0.1 with Single-Use Tokens

Local AI workspaces that bind to 0.0.0.0 expose developer filesystems to LAN and DNS-rebinding attacks. Auralis enforces strict loopback binding, symlink-safe realpath jails, and single-use HMAC approval tokens while indexing at 3,110 docs/sec.

AgentShield

OWASP 2026 AI Agent Security & Capability Firewall

1. System Architecture Blueprint

[Untrusted Context / Prompt]
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Context Taint Scanner (Indirect Injection & Confusion) │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 2. Tool Argument Validator (Path, Shell, SQL, SSRF Guard) │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 3. Capability Gate & HMAC-SHA256 Single-Use Approval Token│
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 4. Secret Redactor (AWS, JWT, PEM, Bearer, Mobile Money)  │
└───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
        [Tamper-Evident SHA-256 Chained Audit Ledger]
  • Context Taint & Prompt Injection Scanner
    Detects role-override instructions, base64/hex obfuscated payloads, and untrusted RAG/webhook taint attempting to invoke high-privilege tools.
  • Deterministic Argument & Egress Inspector
    Blocks RFC1918/link-local/IMDSv2 (169.254.169.254) SSRF targets, path traversal (../), command chaining, and destructive SQL/filesystem payloads.
  • HMAC-SHA256 Capability & Human-in-the-Loop Gate
    Requires cryptographically bound single-use tokens tied to canonical {toolName, argsHash, sessionId} before executing destructive operations.
  • Hash-Chained Audit Ledger
    Links every decision entry via prevHash -> entryHash (SHA-256) so post-compromise log tampering is mathematically detectable.

2. Deterministic Invariants & Safety Boundaries

  • ✓ Zero LLM-in-the-loop latency or non-determinism on security boundaries—all policy checks execute deterministically in sub-millisecond time.
  • ✓ Approval tokens bind to canonicalized JSON argument hashes and cannot be replayed across tools or sessions.
  • ✓ Every output stream passes through multi-pattern secret scrubbing before returning to the model or caller.

3. Key Engineering Trade-Offs (Architecture Decision Records)

ADR-01: Deterministic Capability Inspection Over LLM-Judge Guardrails

CONTEXT: Probabilistic "LLM-as-a-judge" guardrails are themselves vulnerable to adversarial jailbreaks and add 300–1,500 ms of latency per tool call.

DECISION: Enforce strict capability policies, AST/regex structural validators, RFC1918/IMDSv2 IP range parsing, and taint propagation rules purely in deterministic TypeScript.

TRADE-OFFS: Requires explicit policy definitions per tool capability class, but guarantees 0% non-determinism, sub-millisecond overhead, and 100% reproducibility in CI.

VERIFICATION: Verified across 42 unit/integration tests and a 25-scenario OWASP Agentic Top 10 red-team benchmark with 100% recall and 0% false positive rate.

ADR-02: Cryptographic Single-Use Approval Tokens Bound to Canonical Argument Hash

CONTEXT: Boolean confirmation flags in agent loops can be spoofed by prompt injection or replayed with mutated tool arguments.

DECISION: Issue HMAC-SHA256 tokens bound to (toolName, canonicalArgsSha256, sessionId, expiresAt) and mark nonces consumed immediately upon verification.

TRADE-OFFS: Requires the host orchestrator to manage an approval secret and token lifecycle, preventing all parameter-tampering and replay attacks.

VERIFICATION: Tested against token replay, cross-tool substitution, argument mutation, and expiration tampering in tests/agentshield.test.ts.
